_authority: The mandatory asset hierarchy, the source-authority ranking, the rights states and the provenance contract. source/GUIDE.md and scripts/resolve_asset.py both read this. Do not restate its levels in prose elsewhere.
_law: Levels run in order. A level is only exhausted when it has been SEARCHED, not when it has been assumed empty. 'I could not think of one' is not a search.

levels.name: PROJECT
search: any assets the operator supplied with the brief
project manuals, technical drawings, schematics, photographs
the knowledge base's extracted figure artefacts, where a figure is genuinely needed
levels.search_terms_rule: Search by MORE than the words in the request. Expand to: the equipment name, the manufacturer, alternate and older terminology, the system name, the document title, likely figure captions, and the abbreviation. A single failed grep for the requester's phrasing is not a search.
term_expansion_examples: one word -> its plural, its hyphenated and unhyphenated forms, its abbreviation
a component -> the system it belongs to, and the document that would document that system
a modern term -> the term a manual from twenty years earlier would have used
levels.wins_because: a project asset is already cleared, already correct for this operator's equipment, and needs no rights decision

levels.name: FACTORY
levels.reuse_test: Reuse only if it is BOTH technically correct for this subject and pedagogically right for this learning need. A near-miss reused to save time teaches the near-miss.
levels.wins_because: already reviewed, already licence-clean, already tablet-tested

levels.name: INTERNET
levels.gate: only after 1 and 2 have actually been searched and the search recorded

authority_ranking.source: the manufacturer of the actual equipment
a recognised maritime or technical organisation
another credible technical source (a university, a national laboratory, a technical museum)
an open media repository with per-file licence and author metadata

not_authority: personal blogs without a named technical author
any page that does not name where the image itself came from
levels.offline_law: A legally usable internet asset is DOWNLOADED and packaged locally. The tablet has no network at class time and the app returns 403 to every host but the classroom backend. A remote image reference is a broken image on a tablet, not a slow one.

levels.name: CREATE
levels.gate: only when no suitable asset exists at 1-3

choose_by_teaching_need.svg: technical diagrams, systems, piping, valves, tanks, component relationships - anything with topology, labels or state
choose_by_teaching_need.html_css_js: state-based process explanations and controlled interactive behaviour
choose_by_teaching_need.canvas: only where element count or per-frame maths genuinely defeats SVG - and accept that it is invisible to every static check here
choose_by_teaching_need.programmatic: where precision or repeatability matters - generate the geometry from a data structure, not by hand
choose_by_teaching_need.generated_illustration: only when a realistic or illustrative SCENE is genuinely the right educational medium

levels.hard_rule: Do NOT use generated imagery in place of a structured technical schematic. A diagram that must be accurate is authored, not sampled.

rights_states.CLEARED: licence identified, permits this use, attribution requirement recorded and satisfied on the page
rights_states.PROJECT_OWNED: supplied by the operator from their own material - no external licence question
rights_states.ATTRIBUTION_REQUIRED: usable, and the credit line must appear wherever the asset appears
rights_states.RIGHTS_REVIEW_REQUIRED: usage rights unclear, restricted, or a publisher figure that is not cleared for issue. BLOCKS shipping. Escalate to the owner; never resolve it by assumption.
rights_states.REJECTED: found and deliberately not used - record why, so the next search does not repeat it

rights_law: Unclear rights are RIGHTS_REVIEW_REQUIRED, never a silent ship.
An uncleared publisher figure can block an entire course from being issued. That has already happened once in this system.

Acceptable for photographs: public domain, CC0, CC BY, CC BY-SA, or explicit permission. Not acceptable: NC, ND, 'free to use' with no named licence, stock previews, or anything scraped from a manufacturer site or a PDF without a rights decision.
Record the licence per file, beside the file, not in a central register that goes stale.

verification_law.rule: Open and look at every image before using it. Record that you looked, and when.
verification_law.why: A file named for one ship type turned out to show a completely different vessel. A caption is not evidence of content.
verification_law.field: visually_verified must read 'yes - <what was seen> <date>' or state plainly that it was not verified. Never write yes for a file nobody opened.

honesty_rules: Never contradict named equipment. If the course names a manufacturer, the image must show that manufacturer's kit or must not be captioned as it.
Caption a near-miss honestly. 'A product tanker, not a gas carrier' is a usable caption; silence is not.
Never present a generated illustration as a photograph.
Never present an interpolated value as a measured one.

provenance_files.rule: one metadata file per asset folder, keyed by filename, sitting beside the files it describes

naming_and_format.naming: lower snake_case, subject first, no module number, no spaces
naming_and_format.photographs: JPEG, quality ~82, max 2200 px on the long edge
naming_and_format.diagrams: inline SVG wherever the diagram is authored
naming_and_format.why_extensions_matter: the Android WebView serves a fixed MIME allowlist; anything outside it is served as application/octet-stream and will not render
